timing: retrospective specification of previously generated candidate

sourceFacts.fact: Spastic diplegia predominantly affects the legs.
Hemiplegia affects one side; quadriplegia affects all four limbs and may include the trunk and face.

invariants: Diplegia legs emphasized; hemiplegia same-side arm and leg; quadriplegia all four limbs.
Distribution does not encode functional prognosis; maps have no internal anatomy.
expectedLabels: s RIGHT arm and RIGHT leg highlighted ochre, opposite side plain; bottom
: BOTH arms and BOTH legs highlighted muted teal, trunk a lighter wash; bottom
layoutSpecification: Three modest, flat front-facing CHILD BODY MAPS in plain t-shirt and leggings, neutral stance, no actual diagnostic posture. Same size. Left heading 'Diplegia': both legs strongly teal highlighted, arms plain; bottom 'Legs more affected'. Middle 'Hemiplegia': viewer's RIGHT arm and RIGHT leg highlighted ochre, opposite side plain; bottom 'One side affected'. Right 'Quadriplegia': BOTH arms and BOTH legs highlighted muted teal, trunk a lighter wash; bottom 'All four limbs affected'. Title 'Spastic cerebral palsy: distribution'. Small bottom note 'Body maps show distribution, not functional ability'. No chair or walking prediction, no smile/frown severity judgment, no spinal lesion.
forbiddenAnatomy: No claimed anatomical reconstruction, diagnostic image, histology or literal neuroanatomical pathway
No organ cutaways or invented internal spatial relationships

validation.sourceFacts: Checked against listed primary clinical sources during original topic review
validation.pixelChecks: Visually inspected: diplegia map highlights both legs, hemiplegia one ipsilateral arm/leg, quadriplegia all four limbs. Labels match distributions and explicitly distinguish body maps from functional ability; no diagnosis from pose or prognosis implied.
